lasso.default: You shake out a loop and drop it over {the:noun}. Nothing comes of it, and you coil the rope back up.

rules.say: You'd need a rope for that.
That's a good way to get yourself shot.
You shake out a loop and toss it. The mare sidesteps without even hurrying, then watches you coil the rope back in. She won't be rushed.

say.text: This time she stands for it. The loop settles over her neck and she lets you draw it snug.
say.else: You move slowly and let the loop drop over her neck. She flinches and throws her head, but she doesn't run.

rules.say: She's already on the end of your rope.
You hold out a lump on your flat palm. She stretches her neck as far as it will go, takes it, and crunches. You give her the rest. Some of the white goes out of her eye.
You'd need the sugar in your hand first.
You're tempted. But Juniper needs them more than you do.

say.text: She leans her head into your hand.
say.else: She jerks her head away before you can touch her.

rules._note: The soft path: without sugar, patience settles her, at the cost of the whistle, five points and a sore horse.

then.say: She drops her head and starts nosing at a clump of dry grass, as if she has forgotten you. You could likely get a rope on her now.
You stand still and let her look at you. One ear swivels your way.

else.say: She takes a step towards you, thinks better of it, and stops. But she doesn't back away.

rules.say: You swing up bareback, turn her head south and give her her heels. Sorrow Creek is a smudge of dust behind you before you think better of it.
She'd have you in the dirt before you got a leg over.
The sheriff snorts, lifts his hat an inch and says, "Help yourself to the sugar, Ada's been asking." The hat comes down again. He is snoring before you can answer.
The sheriff snorts in his sleep and turns his face to the wall.

say: Ada lets out a whoop that sets every horse in the stable stamping.

say.text: Then she sees the sweat on Juniper's neck where the rope has rubbed, and her mouth goes tight. "Rough way to bring a horse home," she says.
